data.one_liner: Real-time performance monitoring with FPS tracking, memory usage, and CPU monitoring for Flutter.
data.what_it_does: Tracks real-time performance metrics in Flutter applications including FPS, system-level memory, and CPU usage. It provides native implementations for iOS and Android, alongside fallbacks for web and desktop platforms. Developers can display these metrics directly in the UI using a provided widget.
use_when: You need to monitor frame rates and UI performance during development or production.
You want to track memory and CPU usage across Android and iOS platforms.
You need built-in UI components to show real-time performance metrics.
avoid_when: You are targeting environments where native hardware metrics or debug overlays are not desired.
You require detailed profiling tools that go beyond basic real-time metrics.
strengths: Provides native support for memory and CPU usage on Android and iOS.
Includes cross-platform fallback mechanisms for web and desktop platforms.
Easy integration with a ready-to-use widget tree component.
weaknesses: Memory monitoring on web shows 0.0 MB due to browser security restrictions.
CPU usage on desktop and web relies on FPS-based estimations rather than full native processes.
data.setup_notes: Initialize the monitor by calling FlutterPerfMonitor.initialize() in your main function and add PerfMonitorWidget to your widget tree.
